---
title: "Stuff predicts next season better than results do"
description: "A pitch-quality model built only on velocity, movement, and release predicts a pitcher's next season better than his run value does, and it works on Triple-A pitchers too."
date: 2026-11-10
categories: [pitching, models]
image: thumb.png
---

::: {.finding}
[The finding]{.label}
A pitcher's **Stuff+**, graded only on velocity, movement, spin, and release, predicted his {{< meta baseball.season >}} run value better than his {{< meta baseball.season_prev >}} run value did (r = {{< meta baseball.stuff_yoy_r_stuff >}} vs. {{< meta baseball.stuff_yoy_r_results >}}, {{< meta baseball.stuff_yoy_n >}} pitchers). Stuff+ also stabilizes almost immediately, while a season of actual results is still mostly noise.
:::

::: {.so-what}
[So what]{.label}

- **When results and stuff disagree, lean toward the stuff.** A pitcher with good stuff and bad results is a better bet to improve than his ERA suggests, and the reverse holds too.
- **It works on minor leaguers.** For pitchers who moved from Triple-A in {{< meta baseball.season_prev >}} to MLB in {{< meta baseball.season >}}, Triple-A Stuff+ had some signal for big-league results (r = {{< meta baseball.stuff_aaa_r_stuff >}}). Triple-A results had none (r = {{< meta baseball.stuff_aaa_r_results >}}).
- **It tells you what to fix, not just how good a pitcher is.** Because the inputs are physical, a low grade points at a specific shape, velocity, or release issue a coach can work on.
:::

## Last year's stuff vs. last year's results

Each dot is a pitcher with {{< meta baseball.stuff_min_pitches >}}+ pitches in both {{< meta baseball.season_prev >}} and {{< meta baseball.season >}}. Switch the predictor to compare. With Stuff, the trend line is steeper relative to the spread, and the gap between the top and bottom groups is wider.

```{=html}
<div class="explorer">
  <div class="controls" id="c1"></div>
  <div class="plot-host" id="p1"></div>
  <p class="caption" id="cap1"></p>
  <div class="plot-host" id="p2"></div>
  <p class="caption">Pitchers split into five equal groups by the chosen {{< meta baseball.season_prev >}} measure. The wider the spread between the top and bottom groups, the more useful the measure is for predicting {{< meta baseball.season >}}.</p>
</div>
<script>
(async () => {
  const S = Sparvi, f = S.fmt;
  const [yy, meta] = await Promise.all([S.load("/data/baseball/stuff_yoy.json"), S.load("/data/baseball/meta.json")]);
  const st = { x: "xrv100_prev", q: "" };
  const Y = meta.season, P = Y - 1;
  const lab = { xrv100_prev: `${P} Stuff (expected run value per 100 pitches) →`, rv100_prev: `${P} actual run value per 100 pitches →` };
  const r = (k) => S.corr(yy, k, "rv100_cur");
  document.getElementById("c1").replaceChildren(
    S.el("label", {}, `Predict ${Y} with`, S.seg([["xrv100_prev", `${P} Stuff`], ["rv100_prev", `${P} results`]], st.x, v => { st.x = v; draw(); })),
    S.search("Find a pitcher", "Name", v => { st.q = v; draw(); }));
  function draw() {
    const hi = st.q ? yy.filter(d => d.name.toLowerCase().includes(st.q)) : [];
    S.plot(document.getElementById("p1"), w => Plot.plot({ ...S.plotDefaults(w), height: 360, grid: true,
      x: { label: lab[st.x] }, y: { label: `↑ ${Y} actual run value per 100 pitches` },
      marks: [Plot.dot(yy, { x: st.x, y: "rv100_cur", r: 3.5, fill: "#2a78d6", fillOpacity: hi.length ? .2 : .55 }),
        Plot.linearRegressionY(yy, { x: st.x, y: "rv100_cur", stroke: "#16181d", ci: 0.9 }),
        Plot.dot(hi, { x: st.x, y: "rv100_cur", r: 6, fill: "#eb6834", stroke: "#fff", strokeWidth: 1.5 }),
        Plot.text(hi.slice(0, 6), { x: st.x, y: "rv100_cur", text: "name", dy: -12, fontWeight: 600 }),
        Plot.tip(yy, Plot.pointer({ x: st.x, y: "rv100_cur", title: d => `${d.name}\n${P} Stuff ${f.num(d.xrv100_prev, 2)} · ${P} RV ${f.num(d.rv100_prev, 2)}\n${Y} RV ${f.num(d.rv100_cur, 2)}` }))] }));
    document.getElementById("cap1").textContent = `r = ${r(st.x).toFixed(2)} across ${yy.length} pitchers. Positive run value is good for the pitcher. Shaded band: 90% interval on the trend line.`;
    const qs = d3.scaleQuantile().domain(yy.map(d => d[st.x])).range([1, 2, 3, 4, 5]);
    const bins = d3.rollups(yy, v => d3.mean(v, d => d.rv100_cur), d => qs(d[st.x])).map(([q, v]) => ({ q, v })).sort((a, b) => a.q - b.q);
    S.plot(document.getElementById("p2"), w => Plot.plot({ ...S.plotDefaults(w), height: 220, marginLeft: 60,
      x: { label: `${st.x === "xrv100_prev" ? `${P} Stuff` : `${P} results`} quintile →`, tickFormat: d => ["", "Bottom", "2nd", "Middle", "4th", "Top"][d] },
      y: { label: `↑ Avg. ${Y} RV/100`, grid: true },
      marks: [Plot.ruleY([0]), Plot.barY(bins, { x: "q", y: "v", fill: d => d.v >= 0 ? "#eb6834" : "#2a78d6", insetLeft: 12, insetRight: 12, rx: 3 }),
        Plot.text(bins.filter(d => d.v >= 0), { x: "q", y: "v", text: d => f.signed(d.v, 2), dy: -8, fontWeight: 600 }),
        Plot.text(bins.filter(d => d.v < 0), { x: "q", y: 0, text: d => f.signed(d.v, 2), dy: -8, fontWeight: 600 })] }));
  }
  draw();
})();
</script>
```

The difference isn't huge, and it shouldn't be: plenty of what happens next season (injuries, role changes, new pitches) isn't in either number. A bootstrap of the gap between the two correlations gives a 90% interval of {{< meta baseball.stuff_gap_lo >}} to {{< meta baseball.stuff_gap_hi >}}. {{< meta baseball.stuff_gap_sentence >}}

## What the model pays attention to

Importance is spread across many traits rather than dominated by velocity. Averaged across the three models, {{< meta baseball.stuff_top_features >}} carry the most, and {{< meta baseball.stuff_least_feature >}} the least. The mix shifts by pitch type. {{< meta baseball.stuff_gap_mix >}}

```{=html}
<div class="explorer">
  <div class="controls" id="c3"></div>
  <div class="plot-host" id="p3"></div>
  <p class="caption">Share of total gain in each pitch group's model. Gain splits credit between correlated features (velocity and the velocity gap, for example), so read this as "what the model uses," not as causal effects.</p>
</div>
<script>
(async () => {
  const S = Sparvi;
  const imp = await S.load("/data/baseball/stuff_importance.json");
  const nice = { velo: "Velocity", ivb: "Induced vert. break", hb: "Horizontal break", spin: "Spin rate", spin_axis: "Spin axis",
    extension: "Extension", rel_z: "Release height", rel_x: "Release side", arm_angle: "Arm angle",
    velo_diff: "Velo gap vs. fastball", ivb_diff: "IVB gap vs. fastball", hb_diff: "HB gap vs. fastball" };
  let g = "fastball";
  document.getElementById("c3").replaceChildren(S.el("label", {}, "Model", S.seg([["fastball", "Fastballs"], ["breaking", "Breaking balls"], ["offspeed", "Offspeed"]], g, v => { g = v; draw(); })));
  function draw() {
    const d = imp.filter(x => x.group === g).map(x => ({ f: nice[x.feature], v: x.gain * 100 })).sort((a, b) => b.v - a.v);
    S.plot(document.getElementById("p3"), w => Plot.plot({ ...S.plotDefaults(w), height: 330, marginLeft: 150,
      x: { label: "Share of gain (%) →", grid: true }, y: { label: null, domain: d.map(x => x.f) },
      marks: [Plot.barX(d, { x: "v", y: "f", fill: "#0f5257", rx: 2 }), Plot.text(d, { x: "v", y: "f", text: x => x.v.toFixed(1), dx: 16 })] }));
  }
  draw();
})();
</script>
```

## Triple-A

Statcast tracking covers every Triple-A park, so the same model, trained only on MLB pitches, can grade minor leaguers on the same scale. The average qualified Triple-A pitcher grades out around {{< meta baseball.stuff_aaa_mean >}}, a little under one standard deviation below an average big leaguer. For {{< meta baseball.stuff_aaa_n >}} pitchers who threw {{< meta baseball.stuff_aaa_min_pitches >}}+ Triple-A pitches in {{< meta baseball.season_prev >}} and {{< meta baseball.stuff_min_pitches >}}+ MLB pitches in {{< meta baseball.season >}}, Triple-A Stuff+ correlated with MLB run value at r = {{< meta baseball.stuff_aaa_r_stuff >}}, and Triple-A results at r = {{< meta baseball.stuff_aaa_r_results >}}. Both samples are small, but only one of those numbers carried any information.

Every {{< meta baseball.season >}} grade, at both levels and by individual pitch, is in the **[Stuff+ leaderboard](/baseball/tools/stuff-leaderboard.html)**.

<details class="method" id="method">
<summary>Method and caveats</summary>

**Data.** Pitch-level Statcast from Baseball Savant: MLB {{< meta baseball.mlb_span >}} (about {{< meta baseball.stuff_pitches_mlb >}} pitches) and Triple-A {{< meta baseball.aaa_span >}} (about {{< meta baseball.stuff_pitches_aaa >}}).

**Features.** Velocity, induced vertical break, horizontal break, spin rate, spin axis, release height and side, extension, arm angle, and the velocity and movement gaps between each pitch and the pitcher's most-used fastball that season. Lefties are mirrored so arm-side movement is positive for everyone. Location, count, batter, and outcome are deliberately excluded.

**Target.** Run value from the pitcher's side (negative `delta_run_exp`). On balls in play, the actual outcome is swapped for the expected outcome from exit velocity and launch angle, converted to runs with a wOBA scale of 1.24. That strips out defense and batted-ball luck.

**Model.** One LightGBM regressor each for fastballs, breaking balls, and offspeed pitches, with wide leaves (`min_data_in_leaf = 500`) because a single pitch's run value is mostly noise. The published grades come from a model trained on MLB {{< meta baseball.train_span >}} and early-stopped on a 15% holdout of pitchers. The year-over-year test above uses a separate model trained on {{< meta baseball.stuff_yoy_train_season >}} only, so both the {{< meta baseball.season_prev >}} grades and the {{< meta baseball.season >}} results are out of sample.

**Scale.** Stuff+ is a pitcher's average predicted run value per 100 pitches, scaled so 100 is the average qualified ({{< meta baseball.stuff_min_pitches >}}+ pitch) MLB pitcher in {{< meta baseball.season >}} and 10 points is one standard deviation. Pitch-level grades are scaled within pitch group. RV+ applies the same scaling to actual run value.

**Checks.** Pitch-level R² on the {{< meta baseball.season >}} holdout is {{< meta baseball.stuff_holdout_r2 >}}, which is expected because single pitches are coin flips. Split-half reliability within a season is {{< meta baseball.stuff_split_half_stuff >}} for Stuff+ and {{< meta baseball.stuff_split_half_rv >}} for actual run value.

**Not included.** Location and command, count and sequencing, park or tracking-system differences between levels (not corrected), and errors in Savant's pitch-type labels (inherited by the fastball-gap features).

Code: [`baseball/pitch_quality/`](https://github.com/matt-hardman15/sparvi-site/tree/main/baseball/pitch_quality)
</details>
